# h3_database_pooler (Resource)

Manages a connection pooler (PgBouncer) of a PostgreSQL `h3_database`. A database can have several poolers: `rw` (to the primary), `ro` (to the replicas only) and `r` (to every instance), each with its own mode, number of pods, parameters and listeners. `display_name`, `mode`, `instances`, `default`, `paused`, `parameters`, `vpc_mode`, `vpc_port`, `public_port` and `public_via` change in place: PgBouncer pods roll one by one, PostgreSQL is not restarted. `pooler_id`, `role` and `database_id` force a new pooler. Apply waits (up to 10 minutes) until the pooler is `READY` (`PAUSED` with `paused = true`).

Where clients connect: `vpc_mode`/`vpc_port` (inside the project VPC) and `public_port` (on the public EIP of the database, set with `white_ip`/`eip_id` of `h3_database`; the pooler does not lease an EIP). Pooler pods are billed per pod. Needs h3db with several poolers per database enabled for the project (`POOLER_MULTI_DISABLED` otherwise).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Default pooler of the database: transaction mode, two PgBouncer pods, port
# 6432 on the VPC address and on the public EIP of the database.
resource "h3_database_pooler" "main" {
  database_id  = h3_database.pg.id
  pooler_id    = "main" # changing it replaces the pooler
  role         = "rw"   # rw | ro | r; changing it replaces the pooler
  display_name = "main (transaction)"
  mode         = "transaction" # in place: the pods roll, PostgreSQL is not restarted
  instances    = 2
  default      = true

  vpc_mode    = "port" # port | address | none
  vpc_port    = 6432
  public_port = 6432 # needs white_ip = true on the database; 0 removes it

  # Authoritative: a key removed here returns to the h3db default.
  parameters = {
    default_pool_size = "50"
    max_client_conn   = "3000"
  }
}

# Session pooler for reports on the replicas (the database needs a read
# replica or an HA standby), on its own address in the VPC.
resource "h3_database_pooler" "reports" {
  database_id = h3_database.pg.id
  pooler_id   = "reports"
  role        = "ro"
  mode        = "session"
  instances   = 1
  vpc_mode    = "address"
}

output "pooler_endpoints" {
  value = {
    vpc    = h3_database_pooler.main.vpc_endpoint     # e.g. 10.10.0.20:6432
    public = h3_database_pooler.main.public_endpoints # e.g. ["45.93.22.149:6432"]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `database_id` (String) ID of the PostgreSQL `h3_database`
- `pooler_id` (String) Pooler ID, unique in the database: 1-20 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, starting and ending with a letter or digit (e.g. `main`, `ro`, `reports`). The Kubernetes object is `db-<database>-pooler-<pooler_id>`. Changing it replaces the pooler.
- `role` (String) `rw` (the primary), `ro` (read replicas and HA standbys only) or `r` (every instance). `ro` and `r` need at least two instances of the database (`ROLE_NEEDS_REPLICA`). Changing it replaces the pooler.

### Optional

- `default` (Boolean) The default pooler of the database (`rw` only; exactly one). It is the pooler of the older `/pooler` API and of `h3 db pooler get`. Setting `true` moves the flag from the other pooler, whose `default` reads `false` on its next refresh; do not set `true` on two poolers. Not set: chosen by h3db.
- `display_name` (String) Name shown in the console, at most 64 characters. Not set: chosen by h3db. Changed in place.
- `instances` (Number) Number of PgBouncer pods, at least 1. The upper bound is set by h3db (16 today, see `limits.max_instances` of the data source `h3_database_poolers`; `INVALID_INSTANCES`). Not set: the h3db default (2). Changed in place.
- `mode` (String) Pool mode: `session` (the h3db default) or `transaction`. Changed in place (the pods roll; in `transaction` mode session state such as `SET`, advisory locks and `LISTEN` is not kept between transactions).
- `parameters` (Map of String) PgBouncer parameters set by you, as strings (e.g. `{ default_pool_size = "50" }`). Allowed keys: `client_idle_timeout`, `client_tls_sslmode`, `default_pool_size`, `idle_transaction_timeout`, `max_client_conn`, `max_db_client_connections`, `max_db_connections`, `max_prepared_statements`, `max_user_client_connections`, `max_user_connections`, `min_pool_size`, `query_timeout`, `query_wait_timeout`, `reserve_pool_size`, `reserve_pool_timeout`, `server_idle_timeout`, `server_lifetime`. Values are non-negative integers, `client_tls_sslmode` is `require` or `prefer`. The map is authoritative: a key removed from it returns to the h3db default. Ranges and the connection budget of the database (sum of `instances` × `max_db_connections` + 10 within `max_connections`, per instance) are checked by h3db (`INVALID_PARAMETER`, `INVALID_LIMITS`). The values in effect are in `effective_parameters`.
- `paused` (Boolean) `true` pauses the pooler (PgBouncer `PAUSE`: clients stay connected, new queries wait); `false` resumes it. Changed in place.
- `public_port` (Number) Port of the pooler on the public EIP of the database, 1024-65535; `0` removes the public listener. `5432` puts the pooler on the main port of the database (instead of PostgreSQL). Needs a public address of the database (`white_ip = true`, `PUBLIC_NEEDS_EIP`). Not set: no public listener on create, the current one later.
- `public_via` (String) How the public port is set up on the EIP: `port-sources` (the default: a port of the database load balancer) or `service` (a separate load balancer on the same EIP). Changed in place.
- `vpc_mode` (String) Listener in the project VPC: `port` (a port on the VPC address of the database), `address` (an own VPC address of the pooler) or `none`. Not set: h3db chooses (`port` when the database has a VPC address); removing it from the configuration keeps the current value. Changed in place. Free of charge.
- `vpc_port` (Number) Port of the VPC listener, 1024-65535. Not set: the h3db default (6432 for `rw`, 6433 for `ro`, 6434 for `r` with `vpc_mode = "port"`; 5432 with `address`). Not allowed with `vpc_mode = "none"`.

### Read-Only

- `adopted` (Boolean) The pooler was created outside h3db and taken over (older databases).
- `effective_parameters` (Map of String) PgBouncer parameters in effect (yours plus the h3db defaults for the mode, the size of the database and the other poolers).
- `id` (String) `<database_id>/<pooler_id>`
- `k8s_name` (String) Name of the Kubernetes Pooler object (shown in the console under the name).
- `phase` (String) `READY`, `PROGRESSING`, `PAUSED` or `STOPPED` (the database is stopped).
- `public_addresses` (Attributes List) Listeners of the pooler on the public EIP of the database. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--public_addresses))
- `public_endpoints` (List of String) `<ip>:<port>` of the pooler on the public EIP of the database.
- `ready_instances` (Number) Ready PgBouncer pods.
- `vpc_endpoint` (String) `<ip>:<port>` of the pooler in the VPC; null without a VPC listener.
- `vpc_ip` (String) IP of the VPC listener; null without one.
- `vpc_status` (String) State of the VPC listener: `assigned`, `pending` or `unavailable` (the address could not be set up, e.g. the database has no VPC address); null with `vpc_mode = "none"`.

<a id="nestedatt--public_addresses"></a>
### Nested Schema for `public_addresses`

Read-Only:

- `eip_id` (String) Elastic IP ID
- `endpoint` (String) `<ip>:<port>`
- `ip` (String) Public IP (the EIP of the database)
- `port` (Number) Port
- `via` (String) `port-sources`, `service` or `external` (taken over from an older setup)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by <database_id>/<pooler_id>
terraform import h3_database_pooler.main 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555/main
```
